messages:
katie: Heads up — canary publish for Python + TS SDKs is failing on the publish bot, 403 from PyPI during wheel upload. Noticed at 08:42 UTC. Anyone available?

deploy-bot: [AUTOMATED] publish-job #542 failed at 2025-03-21T08:42:13Z
error: HTTP 403 Forbidden uploading to https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/
command: `twine upload dist/*`

sahil: I'm available. Looks like the ephemeral PyPI token expired or got rotated. I'll try to reissue a token and re-run to a staging repository first.

amy: If we re-run, let's avoid stomping the canary tag on npm/pypi. For npm use a temporary dist-tag like `next-temp` and for PyPI publish to test.pypi.org first.

leo: +1 to staging first. If re-run fails, we should rollback the canary and hold GA. Also we should pin the previous canary SHA in the changelog to avoid downstream surprises.

micah: Can someone paste the minimal error log? Want to check if it's creds or project permissions. We've seen org token-scopes mismatch cause this.

katie: log snippet from CI:
```
HTTPError: 403 Client Error: Forbidden for url: https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/
Response: Upload failed - Invalid or expired token
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/bin/twine", line 12, in <module>
    main()
  ...
```

sahil: Ok I reissued a token with `--scope:upload` and attempted a staging push:
`twine upload --repository-url https://test.pypi.org/legacy/ -u __token__ -p <redacted> dist/*`

deploy-bot: publish-job #543 started at 2025-03-21T08:55:03Z
deploy-bot: publish-job #543 failed at 2025-03-21T08:56:11Z — 403 Forbidden (token rejected)

amy: That's 2x 403s, so this is not just a transient TTL. We should follow rollback playbook.

leo: Proposed rollback plan (short):
- mark Python canary as FAILED in release board (do not promote)
- revert published npm dist-tag for TS to previous `canary` target (use `npm dist-tag add <pkg>@<prev> canary`)
- pin SDK version in docs for the change window (call out the hold)
- delay GA cut by 24-48 hours until infra confirms credential/permission fix

micah: I will escalate to infra to check org PyPI token policy & rotate the org token if needed. Also will validate packaging permissions for the project id.

sahil: Once infra rotates, I will test a full publish flow to `test.pypi.org` and a private npm registry staging. If green, we'll attempt a controlled republish.

katie: Who wants release-notes / user-facing message? Need a short blurb explaining: canary failed due to publishing credentials; we're holding GA; will update when republish validated.

leo: I can take release notes. I'll include rollback rationale and an action note about the non-breaking deprecation we planned in the SDK (so customers aren't surprised). I'll open a PR to the release-notes repo and tag the changelog ticket.

amy: Also, add an internal engineer note in the release board: `DO NOT PROMOTE` and include the failed job IDs (#542, #543) and time windows.

micah: ACTIONS: @micah -> rotate org PyPI token + confirm scopes; @sahil -> test publish to staging; @leo -> update release notes PR; @katie -> mark canary as failed and update release board entry. Target: complete within 2 hours (change window). :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sahil: I'll post back with staging results before attempting prod.

katie: OK team. For now: hold GA, rollback canary tags where applicable, update release notes, and coordinate token rotation. I'll ping support to preempt incoming tickets.

leo: sending changelog PR shortly.

amy: Done triage on the release board, added `hold` flag and pinned previous release commit.

katie: Thanks everyone — closing thread after infra confirms rotation and staging publish passes. :thumbsup:
